hypothesis: Machine learning and data-driven approaches are increasingly being used to enhance climate adaptation strategies by improving predictions and understanding of climate impacts, particularly in agriculture, while also being applied in other domains such as biodiversity monitoring and infrastructure resilience. These methods help in estimating the degree of adaptation to climate change by analyzing economic outcomes and agricultural yields, as well as in monitoring biodiversity through citizen science and remote sensing technologies. Furthermore, machine learning aids in the development of infrastructure resilience and informs policy decisions, contributing to more effective climate adaptation strategies.
